newsitem.title: USA: Republicans see aid for families in budget bills.
newsitem.headline: Republicans see aid for families in budget bills.

text.p: Republican Sen. Judd Gregg of New Hampshire said Saturday the congressional action to cut taxes and approve a plan to balance the federal budget was "a positive step" for families.
In the Republican response to President Clinton's weekly radio address, Gregg urged voters to ignore those who said the party did not get everything it wanted in the budget deal with the White House.

"They (the tax and spending bills) move us down the road -- actually, quite a way down the road, toward balancing the budget by the year 2002, something the Congress and the president have agreed on, something we all want," Gregg said.
"Congress is making progress on issues that matter to our families, our seniors, working Americans and our country," he said.
Both the House and Senate gave initial approval to two key budget bills before they adjourned for the Fourth of July holiday recess.
The Senate tax bill would cut taxes a net $77 billion through 2002 and the House would cut taxes a net $85 billion over the same period.

The House and Senate both approved a five-year plan to reduce government spending. While there were major differences in the details, both plans would find their largest savings through a $115 billion five-year reduction in spending on Medicare health care programmes.
